title: On the Credibility of Evaluating LLMs using Survey Questions
benchmark_measurement: Attitudes towards the role of religion in society and religious values, as part of the broader World Value Survey.
findings: The paper's findings are methodological and do not focus on religion specifically. Religion is mentioned as one of the value domains covered in the World Value Survey, and a religious belief is used as an example to illustrate correlated opinions (e.g., belief in religion's role and views on mothers staying at home). The main conclusions are about how prompting (direct vs. chain-of-thought) and decoding (greedy vs. sampling) strategies significantly affect the evaluation of an LLM's value alignment with human populations.
